analysis_notes.bechina_language_note: The word 'בחינת' does not appear anywhere in the Torah #229 source text. The Torah uses: (1) 'מְסֻגָּלִים' (propitious/having a segulah quality) — a descriptive attribute, not a bechina equivalence; (2) 'מְרֻמָּז בַּפָּסוּק' (hinted in the verse) — a homiletical link, not a bechina; (3) 'עַל־יְדֵי ... עַל־יְדֵי זֶה' (through ... through this comes) — explicit eitza (cause-effect) language. The entire logical structure of the Torah is eitza: having the right wood (cause) produces the segulah of childbearing (effect). There is no declaration that any two concepts share the same essential nature.
analysis_notes.teaching_structure: Torah #229 is a purely eitza teaching. Its argument: certain trees, when fashioned into a bed, possess a segulah (propitious power) for having and raising children (and conversely for the opposite). This is supported by a verse (Genesis 43:7) and Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 91). The entire Torah is a single cause-effect statement with scriptural support — it has no bechina substructure.
